question_answers.question: identity/scope
question_answers.answer: THE river-rail interchange: BTS Silom S6 on Taksin Bridge over Sathorn Pier, spanning Sathon, Bang Rak and a Khlong San slice; the app's primary district is Sathon, not Bang Rak as the brief assumed.

question_answers.question: everyday experience
question_answers.answer: Daily life orbits the pier-station nexus: trains, boats, riverside hotel lobbies and Charoen Krung frontage; residential quiet lives a block inland and across the river.

question_answers.question: values+mechanisms
question_answers.answer: Transport 9 comes from the unique BTS-boat pairing; vibe 9 from the riverfront hotel/heritage skyline (State Tower et al.); food 8 from hotel and Charoen Krung dining rather than market streets.

question_answers.question: counter-evidence
question_answers.answer: Green 8/5.2 ha is ungrounded in any named park; the single-platform bottleneck structurally caps peak capacity; the 'ghost tower' keeps a dead landmark on the riverside skyline.

question_answers.question: rhythm
question_answers.answer: Weekday boat-rail peaks with known queue pain; weekend tourist flows through the pier; evenings shift to hotel rooftops and the riverside.

question_answers.question: walkability
question_answers.answer: Compact station-pier connection at street level with Charoen Krung frontage; no walking-duration figures derived here from catchment radius.

question_answers.question: daily life
question_answers.answer: Groceries and essentials spread between Charoen Krung and Sathorn-side blocks; 20 temples and 5 piers in the app facts reflect the river parishes and ferry landings; nightlife is hotel-anchored.

question_answers.question: affordability vs stated figures
question_answers.answer: App 24,000/52,500 sits inside the wide listing band but the source base is weak and internally contradictory (one nearby 1-bed at 24,500; platform aggregates spanning ~8k-45k); treat as editorial, low-end corroborated.

question_answers.question: green/quiet with polygon honesty
question_answers.answer: 5.2 ha cannot be matched to a named park in sources; the river itself and under-bridge gardens plausibly drive the perception; the quiet west-bank 23.5% slice helps the low crowd score.

question_answers.question: conditional fit
question_answers.answer: Strong fit for car-free commuters who value boats + BTS and river-facing living; poor fit for bargain rents or for anyone who needs guaranteed 6-car peak trains.

question_answers.question: recent changes 2024-2026
question_answers.answer: Body-read sources show no completed 2024-2026 infrastructure change: the capacity fix remains cancelled/stalled; operator routes as of retrieval show weekday-only yellow/red/green lines to Sathorn; press mentions of pier-hub policy and fleet renewal lack fetchable URLs (open issue).

question_answers.question: uncertainties/outside-the-score
question_answers.answer: Unresolved: 5.2-ha park composition, the 2024 Sathorn Unique sale-rumour episode (identity now body-read), station upgrade status, rent-stat quality; anchors verified clean against OSM.

editorial.preview: Bangkok's river-rail hinge: one BTS platform on a bridge, a dozen boat lines below, and a riverside skyline of hotels, domes and one famous ruin.
editorial.guide_lead: Saphan Taksin is where the BTS network meets the Chao Phraya: a single-platform station on Taksin Bridge above Sathorn Pier, with Sathon, Bang Rak and a slice of Khlong San in its catchment — a transport-first address whose riverside glamour and residential quiet sit a few blocks apart.

strengths.text: The boat interchange is unmatched: yellow, green-yellow and red express-boat lines terminate at Sathorn, with tourist boats, Thai Smile Boat, a 3.50-baht cross-river ferry and ICONSIAM shuttles alongside BTS.
Riverside identity at street level — State Tower's rooftop cluster and the pier's hotel belt give the area a skyline-and-water rhythm few station areas have.

tradeoffs.text: The single-platform, single-track layout structurally restricts Silom Line capacity and caps trains at 5 cars; the 2017 widening plan has been cancelled, leaving the bottleneck in place.
The green score rides on 5.2 ha no source can name, and the derelict Sathorn Unique tower stands about 200 m from the station with no recorded path to completion.

day_night.text: Days run on commuter and boat-transfer traffic with tourist pulses at the pier; nights belong to hotel rooftops and the riverside, while the inland residential blocks and the west-bank slice go quiet.

within_area_variation.text: The pier-station nexus is loud and busy; Charoen Krung frontage softens toward cafes and hotels; the cross-river Khlong San share of the catchment is a different, quieter world.

conditional_fit.text: Choose it if your week is boats-and-BTS — river commuters and island-bound tourists get the city's best water-rail pairing with no car needed.
Skip it if you need cheap rents (listing evidence is thin and premium-leaning), guaranteed peak train capacity, or measurable green space — all three wobble in this pass.

uncertainties.text: Unresolved: which objects make up the 5.2-ha park figure; the 2024 Sathorn Unique sale-rumour episode (tower identity is body-read, the sale talk is not); any 2024-2026 pier upgrade (policy reports lack fetchable URLs); rent statistics conflict across platforms; anchors verified against OSM with no mismatch.

open_issues: Park composition for park_ha 5.2 (green 8): no named park with a hectare figure found; recommend polygon audit (possible aggregation of slivers/water-edge polygons).

Sathorn Unique tower: identity, location and 'on hold' status now body-read (Wikipedia EN); the 2024 rumoured sale and its denial remain snippet-only — find a dated body-read source before any editorial use of the sale story.
Station capacity project: 'cancelled' per Thai Wikipedia without an as-of date; a 2024-2026 decision (or the BEM-to-BMA design handover) needs a dated source.
Press reports of pier-hub upgrades and Chao Phraya Express Boat fleet renewal (2024-2026) surfaced only in URL-less search summaries; excluded from claims.
Rent: no body-readable aggregate for Sathon khet; app 24,000/52,500 is editorial — recommend the rent-audit follow-up add a Sathon-specific source.
Brief-vs-app district mismatch: brief said 'Bang Rak blend', app says primary district sathon (47.1%) — coordinator should confirm which blend the rent figure encodes.

Orange-flag boat service: operator site lists Nonthaburi-Wat Rajsingkorn (Mon-Fri) and does not show Sathorn as a stop; historical/wiki sources say orange serves Sathorn — route status needs confirmation.
